answer: Agents train a terrain model to predict each mesh vertex over a mesa and nearby karst. To limit sybil model poisoning, the buyer compares contributors' accumulated gradient directions and clusters highly correlated histories. It clips each update and caps the total aggregation weight of each cluster, rather than granting every account equal weight. A swarm sending aligned malicious updates must share that cap instead of multiplying its influence. Diverse attacks can evade clustering, and honest agents with similar data may be grouped together.
